chunks: We never sent a messenger who did not speak the tongue of his people, that he may explain to them distinctly. God leads whosoever He wills astray, and shows whoever He wills the way: He is all-mighty and all-wise.
ai.seo_question: Why did prophets speak the language of their people according to the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Ibrahim underscores the principle of *balagha* (clear communication), noting that prophets were sent in the vernacular of their people to ensure the message was accessible and comprehensible. It further highlights divine sovereignty in guidance (*hidayah*) and misguidance (*tabyir*), affirming Allah's attributes of Might (*Al-Aziz*) and Wisdom (*Al-Hakim*). In Shia exegesis, this is often linked to the necessity of the Prophet Muhammad's clarity in delivering the message of Imamate and divine law.
